subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific public URL/domain/path denylist or warnlist, or fold this into a broader cross-tool egress/security policy?
rationale: The request would create operator-facing security/config surface, and related open items show competing browser-only, web-tool, and private-network policy scopes that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design browser policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy profiles, defaults, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into generic egress policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 canonical if maintainers want one policy for browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP egress.

options.title: Reject core denylist surface
options.body: Close this direction and document that current hostname allowlist/private-network controls are the supported browser navigation policy.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy profiles, defaults, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest browser SSRF/default-hardening history for the policy boundary this issue would extend.
